content.headline: Cooked over fire, poured over rye
content.subheadline: Ember & Rye is a forty-seat dining room built around a wood-burning hearth and a bar that takes whiskey seriously. Dinner Tuesday through Sunday; the fire gets lit at three.
content.imageAlt: The bar at night — bottles backlit under warm pendant lights

content.headline: Tonight's favorites
content.subheadline: Three things people cross the city for. The full menu changes with the seasons; these don't leave.

reviews.quote: The ribs come off the fire like they have somewhere better to be. We've been back four times in two months.
reviews.author: Renata M.

reviews.quote: A bar that lists its rye by farm and vintage, in a room lit like a campfire. My favorite date spot in Logan Square.
reviews.author: Devon C.

reviews.quote: They took our party of nine on a Friday, split the checks without sighing, and the mushroom pot pie converted a steak guy.
reviews.author: Priya S.

items.question: Do you take walk-ins?
items.answer: Always — the bar and the six hearth seats are held for walk-ins every night. The dining room is mostly reservations, but early and late walk-ins usually land a table.

items.question: Can you handle allergies and dietary needs?
items.answer: Yes. The menu marks vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free dishes, and the kitchen will adapt most plates — tell your server, or note it on your reservation.

items.question: Is there parking?
items.answer: Street parking on Kedzie and the side streets, and we're a block from the Logan Square Blue Line stop. The bike corral out front is ours.

content.headline: The hearth seats go first
content.subheadline: Six stools face the fire. If you want to watch your dinner cook, say so when you book.

content.headline: Twelve seats grew into a dining room
content.subheadline: Ember & Rye started as a twelve-seat supper club in a Logan Square walk-up. The hearth came from a farmhouse in Galena; the rye list started as one shelf.

children.text: We cook almost everything over oak and cherry — not because it's fashionable, but because fire makes you pay attention. There's no walk-away setting on a hearth. The menu is short on purpose: a dozen dishes we can stand behind on a Saturday at nine, sourced from farms we can name without checking.

The bar carries about ninety ryes and bourbons, poured honest. If you don't know where to start, tell the bartender what you drink at home and how brave you're feeling — that conversation is the whole wine list speech, and it works better.

content.headline: Come sit by the fire
content.subheadline: Dinner Tuesday through Sunday from five. The hearth seats are first come, first flame.

content.headline: Reserve a table
content.subheadline: Tell us when you're coming and how many; we confirm by email the same day. Parties of seven or more, give us a ring instead.

content.headline: Hours & directions
content.note: The bar and hearth seats are walk-in only, every night. Kitchen takes last orders 45 minutes before close.

content.headline: Request a table
content.description: We confirm by email the same day — this isn't instant booking yet, a human checks the book.
content.successMessage: Request received — we'll confirm by email today. If it's for tonight, call us instead.

items.question: What about large parties?
items.answer: Seven to fourteen guests eat family-style at the harvest table — call and we'll plan the menu together. Beyond fourteen, that's a buyout conversation and we're happy to have it.

items.question: What if I'm running late?
items.answer: We hold tables fifteen minutes, longer if you call. After that the hearth seats become fair game — but we'll always try to fit you back in.
